hyp_1.title: Telemetry tracking loss
hyp_1.explanation: Client-side event tracking dropped events so reported metrics fell.

history.reason: Under active analysis; evidence ev_1_dc77 recorded (supports).
event_volume_check result supports the hypothesis (independent volume view agrees with the first finding) [rule: 2+ supporting items from 2+ analyses, significant after correction]

hyp_2.title: Code regression in a release
hyp_2.explanation: A recent release introduced a bug that broke part of checkout.

history.reason: Under active analysis; evidence ev_2_f167 recorded (supports).
error_analysis result supports the hypothesis (failed orders concentrate on one device segment) [rule: 2+ supporting items from 2+ analyses, significant after correction]

hyp_3.title: Traffic mix shift
hyp_3.explanation: The mix of arriving users shifted toward lower-converting segments.

history.reason: mix_shift_decomposition result contradicts the hypothesis (mix effect 0.000405 explains little of -0.032)

hyp_4.title: Third-party outage
hyp_4.explanation: An external payment dependency failed for a short period.

history.reason: Under active analysis; evidence ev_4_0f16 recorded (supports).

spike_check result supports the hypothesis (failure rate spikes to 0.33 on 2026-09-29 versus 0.15 overall (single abnormal day, raw p=0.00095)) [rule: 2+ supporting items from 2+ analyses, significant after correction]

hyp_5.title: Seasonality or calendar effect
hyp_5.explanation: The comparison window covers weekends or holidays that are normally quieter.

history.reason: seasonal_baseline result contradicts the hypothesis (deviation from same-weekday baseline remains (p=6.26e-14) or no weekday pattern (p=0.857))

hyp_6.title: Natural variation
hyp_6.explanation: The change is within normal day-to-day variation of the metric.

history.reason: change_point result contradicts the hypothesis (a change point exists (p=0.002))

hyp_7.title: Pricing or policy change
hyp_7.explanation: A price or policy change reduced conversion.

hyp_8.title: Gradual cohort decay
hyp_8.explanation: Retention is eroding gradually across cohorts.

history.reason: retention_comparison result contradicts the hypothesis (retention is stable)

supported_causes.statement: Telemetry tracking loss (tracking_loss) is supported by the evidence; its contribution to the observed change could not be quantified.

The evidence is consistent with Code regression in a release (code_regression); the available tools cannot confirm the underlying cause, accounting for about 9% of the observed change (estimate -0.2826 +/- 0.064 SE, method difference_in_differences:exposed_share_weighted).
The evidence is consistent with Third-party outage (third_party_outage); the available tools cannot confirm the underlying cause; its contribution to the observed change could not be quantified.

ruled_out.title: Seasonality or calendar effect

ruled_out.title: Natural variation

ruled_out.title: Gradual cohort decay
